PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior with one Arrange-Act-Assert. RATIONALE: Single responsibility reduces ambiguity when failures occur. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant requires exactly one Act operation or one Arrange-Act-Assert. DECISION RULES: (1) Count distinct Act operations. This method calls Max.max twice (once for n==0 and once for n==390) — >1 Act => non-compliant. (2) Test name does not help; (3) There are clearly multiple assertion scenarios in the same method. VERDICT: non-compliant because the method mixes two separate behaviors (n==0 happy path and n>bounds exception) in a single test method.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should not depend on other tests. RATIONALE: Enables parallel and order-independent execution. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of @Before/@After or only local variables. DECISION RULES: No @Before/@After annotations are present but the test uses only local variables and does not modify shared/static state. VERDICT: compliant because the test uses only local state and does not rely on other tests or shared mutable state.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: For each method under test provide happy and error path tests. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness by checking exceptional behavior separately. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Requires at least two test methods (happy and error). DECISION RULES: The class contains only a single @Test method; per rules, if class has <2 test methods it likely only covers happy path and should be marked non-compliant. Although this method exercises both a happy path and an error path inside the same test, the evaluation requires separate test methods for those flows. VERDICT: non-compliant because error and happy scenarios are combined in one test method rather than provided as separate tests.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate boundary inputs like 0 and out-of-range values. RATIONALE: Boundaries are frequent sources of bugs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of boundary inputs such as 0 or out-of-range values. DECISION RULES: The test explicitly checks n==0 and also attempts a very large n beyond array length (n==390). VERDICT: compliant because the test includes a zero-bound case and an out-of-bounds scenario.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and reuse helpers for duplication. RATIONALE: Reduces duplication and improves maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of helper methods or constants or brevity without duplication. DECISION RULES: There is no duplicated code across multiple tests (only one test exists) and the method is self-contained. VERDICT: compliant because with a single test method there is no harmful duplication and the method is self-contained; extracting helpers would be beneficial but is not required here.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small (<20 lines) and simple. RATIONALE: Simpler tests are easier to maintain and less buggy. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if <20 lines and no loops/complex conditionals; non-compliant if >30 lines or complex. DECISION RULES: Method length is between ~20-30 lines and includes multiple logical blocks (two distinct scenarios); although there are no loops, it exceeds the suggested compactness and mixes flows. When in doubt choose non-compliant. VERDICT: non-compliant because the test is larger and more complex than the recommended small, single-scenario test.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be comprehensive and verify multiple properties. RATIONALE: Superficial assertions can miss faults. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Compliant if assertions check multiple properties (2-3) of results. DECISION RULES: This test uses assertNull for one scenario and a single assertTrue check inside the exception catch to check instance type — superficial coverage of properties. VERDICT: non-compliant because assertions do not verify multiple relevant properties of returned objects for a typical successful scenario; the test focuses on null and exception existence only.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid ignored or disabled tests. RATIONALE: Ignored tests provide no value. EVALUATION CRITERIA: No @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test. DECISION RULES: No such annotations or commented-out tests exist in the provided method/class. VERDICT: compliant because all tests are active and runnable (no @Ignore/@Disabled nor commented-out tests).

PRINCIPLE: Tests should link to requirements. RATIONALE: Traceability aids impact analysis. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of annotations or Javadoc mentioning requirement IDs. DECISION RULES: The class Javadoc explicitly references requirements (RQ-DS-MAX-001, RQ-DS-MAX-002). VERDICT: compliant because traceability is present in class-level documentation.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain 'why' for complex logic. RATIONALE: Useful comments improve maintainability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Minimal, meaningful comments and no commented-out code.
